Commentary.Commentary: What about Sri Lanka? Close to 300 after being ASKED to bat. It is not a bad score at all but not totally enough either. Disciplined bowling might induce some false strokes and eventually wickets. Let's see how they respond with the ball. The new cherry will be the key, as Tim Southee showed...

Probably a day where the surface quickens up? That would be helpful for the Kiwis as the ball will come onto the bat nicely. The batsmen need to get more than just starts and make good use of the conditions.
Quick work done by the Kiwis. Just taken 3 overs this morning to wrap the innings up, for just 7 runs. Dickwella tried to get some quick runs but unfortunately, Kumara could not hang around much.

OUT! Caught at leg gully! That is a sharp catch. Tim Southee gets a 6-fer. Smart bit of captaincy. Williamson positioned a man at leg gully and the ball has gone straight to him. Full and around middle and leg, Kumara looks to flick but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat towards leg gully. Colin de Grandhomme makes no mistake. SRI LANKA BOWLED OUT FOR 282!
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Another bouncer, ducked under again.
A bouncer around middle, Kumara ducks.
On a length around off, solidly defended.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Backs a long way to the leg side and slashes hard but misses.
Full and outside off, driven down the ground. Good diving stop by Colin de Grandhomme at mid off.
Gets a long way across and looks to flick but misses.
Backs away and punches this behind point for a couple.
FOUR! Lucky! Full on middle, Dickwella gets across, looks to paddle but the ball hits the inner half of the bat and goes over the slips towards third man!
Full and outside off, left alone.
Trent Boult to bowl from the other end. 26-6-77-1 so far.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

The batsman has driven it through mid on.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.

The players are out in the middle then. How long before this gets wrapped up? Lahiru Kumara has joined Niroshan Dickwella in the middle. Tim Southee to start off proceedings for the weekend. Here we go...

Russel Arnold now gets some time to spend with Dimuth Karunaratne. Karunaratne says that it is a good score. Adds that it was very difficult to bat on initially but then got easier to bat on. Reckons that Dickwella can score some quick runs and if they manage to get 300, it will be a good total. On his own batting, Dimuth says that he takes his time till the first 15 overs and then starts playing his shots. On missing out on a century, DK says that he does not want to focus on that but also admits that he lost focus and concentration when he got out.

Styris now has a chat with Tim Southee. The latter says that he has played a number of times at Basin and the new ball is always crucial. Adds that after that two guys got in and it became difficult to get wickets. Says that during that time, the Kiwis switched to plan B and bowl shorter stuff which seemed to work well. On being asked as to when do they decide to switch plans, Tim says that it boils down to experience. Styris now asks about plans for different batsmen and one's own strength - how to marry both? Southee smiles and says that it is a good question and smartly deflects that, by saying that players need to do a bit of both.

PITCH REPORT - Scott Styris doing the pitch report observes that it has browned off a little but there are hardly any footmarks, so the spinners will not come into play. However, there are some indentations bound by some grass, which could create some indifferent bounce.

WEATHER REPORT - Friday was stunning. Saturday is not less stunning either. Not a cloud in the sky and the only thing accompanying the vast blue surface above is that small circular thing in yellow - the hot sun which is high and shining.

A real gritty day of cricket was what Friday provided us. First, Tim Southee ran through the top order before you could prepare a cup of tea and then Mathews, Karunaratne and Dickwella fought back. The game is now poised at a stage where both teams would be reasonably happy but this first half an hour would be extremely crucial. If Sri Lanka can manage to get close to 300, the Kiwis could have their hands full. Hello and a warm welcome to the second day of the opening Test between New Zealand and Sri Lanka in Wellington.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Logically and honestly, it might just be a matter of minutes before the innings is wrapped up on Day 2. But you never know with these 'I-don't-have-anything-to-lose' knocks. If Dickwella manages to hang around for 30 minutes or more, you can never predict Sri Lanka's final total. Join us at 11 am local time (2200 GMT, previous night) for all the action from Sunday. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

A bit of a see-saw day for the Kiwis. Tim Southee started brilliantly, taking 3 quick wickets and then came back to register a 5-fer but New Zealand will admit that they have not been at their clinical best. The highly consistent Boult and Wagner struggled and in the final session, bowled too many loose balls.

Niroshan Dickwella has been the centre of attraction so far. He came in at the fall of his skipper, at 167/5 and has not let it go away. After Mathews departed, he has taken the onus upon himself and added 88 runs with three partners so far, which could be very crucial in the context of this game. Without anyone noticing, he has moved to 73 and a century would mean that Sri Lanka cross 300, which could be a very good total on this surface.

Overall, New Zealand's day but Sri Lanka will share the spoils. They were looking down and out at 9/3 but since then, they fought really hard. The 133-run stand between Mathews and Karunaratne shored things up while a bit of a rearguard action has ensured that it was not a meek surrender.
Wow. Just wow. If you are Dickwella or Rajitha, you would be wondering - what just happened. The 9th wicket pair was looking good but just a lapse in concentration has seen a wicket go down.

OUT! A wicket on the last ball of the day. Loose shot from Rajitha. After having seen off so many deliveries, he falls to the final one of the day. Boult eventually gets a wicket. Full length delivery outside off, Rajitha looks to drive but gets an outside edge towards Watling who takes a comfortable catch. THAT WILL ALSO BE STUMPS ON DAY 1.

Good length delivery outside off, the left-hander lets it go.

Outside off, left alone.

Tim Southee is back on as well. 22-6-59-5 so far.

NOT OUT! Umpire's call saves Rajitha. Length delivery on leg, Rajitha looked to flick but got hit on the pads. Boult appealed but the umpire shook his head. Boult felt it was close and convinced Williamson to go for the review. Ball tracking was taking a long time to come and the third umpire almost ruled the decision as not out. However, they did get the technology in the end. That shows the impact is in line but it is clipping the top of the stumps, which means umpire's call would stay and New Zealand retain their review.
HOWZZAT??? Has Boult got one, LBW? Has it pitched outside leg? New Zealand feel this is gone and Williamson wants a second opinion.
Full on middle, the southpaw flicks it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen take a run.
Good length delivery on off, Dickwella defends off the back foot.
Full on middle, the left-hander drives it towards mid on. The batsmen decide against the run.
Good length delivery outside off, Dickwella offers no shot.
The second new ball is due. AND IT IS IMMEDIATELY TAKEN. Trent Boult to make the first use of it. 22-6-66-0 so far.
Around off, pushed down the ground.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Just over! Flighted outside off, Dickwella jumps out of his crease and drags it over mid on. The fielder thinks he has a chance, rushes across to his left and leaps but the ball eludes him.

Full and outside off, Dickwella looks to play the reverse sweep but misses. The ball kisses the bottom edge and goes past the keeper behind. Two runs taken.

Outside off, left alone.
Around off, punched wide of mid on. KR thinks about the single but then sends Dickwella back.
The batsman has dug out that yorker at the last second.
Outside off, much fuller, Kasun feels for it and gets beaten.

FOUR! Nice way to get to your half century! A crucial innings by Dickwella. Playing with controlled aggression and he is actually batting well with the tail here. You never know, how crucial will these runs turn out to be in the end. A short ball outside off, Dickwella waits for the ball and then ramps it over the keeper to the third man fence.

Backs away and steers a full ball but straight to backward point.

Ohohohoho.... ND gets right in line to scoop this delivery but perhaps telegraphed his intentions a bit too early. Boult spots that and bowls it very full, in line of the stumps. Dickwella has to defend.

Landed outside off, Dickwella runs it down towards third man. Colin de Grandhomme dives to his right from backward point and takes some sting off the ball - but Niroshan is not even thinking about the single.

A short ball, pulled towards deep mid-wicket. They do not run.

OUT! That is a fantastic catch from Henry Nicholls! It is never easy to run with the helmet on and that too, backwards. But Nicholls has kept his eye on the ball and taken a stunner. A short ball, outside off, Lakmal looks to pull but is done in by the bounce. Gets a top edge and it balloons in the air, around mid-wicket. There are two men running back - Nicholls from short leg and someone else from short mid-wicket. Eventually, the former calls, goes for it and then dives in the end to take a superb catch. Wagner has his second. Has had to toil hard.
A short ball, around leg, Dickwella plays a half-jab, half pull, into the ground and it bounces over short leg. A single taken. Moves to 40 from just 47 balls.
Much better from Boult. Springs in that surprise full ball. Suranga drives it towards cover.

DID THAT CARRY? Not sure. On a length around off, Dilruwan looked to defend but got a thick inside edge onto his thighs. The ball went behind and Bradley Watling dived to his right. Hard to say whether the ball hit the glove first and died down or went down and then hit the glove.

OUT! Mathews goes now! No century for him either! New Zealand have gone bang bang since Tea. Second wicket in the space of 4 overs and both the important batters are gone. Attacking is fine but perhaps Mathews showed lesser awareness of the game here. New Zealand were bowling to a plan and they were attacking him with the short ball. He could have left those alone, at least for some period after Tea. But the instinct to score runs and not back off has consumed him. This short ball is pitched outside leg and Mathews cannot resist the pull shot. Is cramped for room and gets a top edge. Simple catch for Bradley Watling and it is a Michelle for Southee. His 8th Test 5-fer, 1st at Wellington and second against Sri Lanka overall.
Again a short ball, this time a controlled pull shot is played, towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

OFF THE GLOVE, OVER THE KEEPER! FOUR! Fortuitous period for the Lankans. A short ball, down the leg side, Dickwella looks to pull but is cramped for room. Gets a bit of a glove and it just eludes a leaping Watling to the fine leg fence.
Way down the leg side, Angelo misses his flick. 14 from that over!

EDGED, FOUR! More luck for Mathews. Full and outside off, Angelo makes a feeble-looking poke and gets an outside edge as there is no feet movement. However, there is no slip and the ball races to the third man fence past the diving Bradley Watling! Mathews moves to 83 with that.
Full and outside off, Niroshan punches this through the covers. Finds the gap and gets three runs. The stand is worth 11 from 8 balls.
Goes fuller, Dickwella pushes it towards mid-wicket.
Another short ball, another pull shot. This time more in control. Towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

TOP EDGE, SIX! New Zealand are attacking Sri Lanka but the latter are counter-attacking. Could be an entertaining period of 30 minutes coming up. The ball is pitched around middle, Mathews looks to pull but the bounce does him in. Takes the top edge and fine leg seems interested. But then, realizes that it is flying. Way over his head.
Down the leg side, Dickwella misses his tuck. A productive over for Southee.

Right. Into the wicket-keeper now. Niroshan Dickwella strides out to the middle. Likes to live on the edge. Suddenly, you could see the Lankans raise up their 200 in the next half an hour if he is there. Else, you might see Dilruwan out in the middle during that period as well. The batsmen crossed, so Mathews will be on strike.

OUT! Chandimal falls immediately after Tea! Southee has his fourth and Sri Lanka are in trouble again. Half the side is back in the hut. A short ball, around off, Dinesh looked to pull but was not in control of that shot. The height and bounce got big on him and a top edge was induced. Ajaz Patel at deep mid-wicket waited and waited and waited and cupped the catch safely. Early success for the hosts after the break. Can they run through the lower order now?

Excellent bowling from the Kiwis. They have not got much help in the second session but still did not allow the Lankans to get off the hook. With the ball now reversing, they will be looking to prize out a wicket or two quickly after Tea and then have the tail at their mercy. Join us back at 4 pm local (0300 GMT). 34 overs left, so it is going to be a long session...

No prizes for saying that the Mathews-Chandimal stand is the key for the Lankans but the latter is eating up too many deliveries. He is certainly not comfortable, scoring just 6 from 32 balls, in a stand worth 57 deliveries. Mathews has not got frustrated as yet - but there might come a time when he might.
Sri Lanka's session, without a doubt. 94 runs scored, in 29 overs, for the loss of Karunaratne. They have the foundation for a big score but as was said at Lunch, they have a big tail.
A bouncer around middle, Chandimal ducks. TEA ON DAY 1, SRI LANKA ARE 167/4!
He is taking on Southee even in these dying moments before Tea. Another short ball, pulled with total control, this time behind square leg for a run.

The stand between Mathews and Karunaratne is currently worth 64 and both batsmen are looking increasingly confident and assured. At the same time, the Kiwis have not bowled badly. Only Wagner has tried a bit too hard and leaked some runs. As the great Geoffrey Boycott says - add 2 wickets to the current score and then see how it is looking. The Lankan tail is a big one and a wicket or two quickly after Lunch can derail them. Sri Lanka need two mammoth knocks. Period. New Zealand need to be disciplined. There is plenty on the pitch for the bowlers. Join us back at 1.40 pm local (0040 GMT).

At that stage, it looked like the Lankans might get bowled out in the first session itself. But Mathews, along with his experience and Karunaratne, using his composure, have ensured that we have some contest.
A great session of cricket - with two halves. The first 30 minutes was all New Zealand. The remaining, have seen a wonderful fightback from Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Scott Styris having a look at the track observes that it has a good green tinge of grass but not that green as Wellington is used to see. Reckons that in the past, Day 1 tends to be slow and then the pitch quickens up as the game progresses. However, because the county has been devoid of first-class cricket this season, the pitch should nip around from today itself, he reckons.

Sri Lankan skipper, Dinesh Chandimal too, wanted to bowl first as he opines that there is a bit of moisture on the wicket. On Sri Lanka as a team for this challenge, Chandimal points out that the last 2 series were played at home but also reminds us that the last time the Lankans played out of home, in the Caribbean, it were the seamers who got them the victory.

New Zealand captain, Kane Williamson, says that the reason to bowl is because there is a bit of grass on the wicket. Hopes that his side bowls in the right areas. On the jet lag of travelling from the Middle East, Kane looks worried but is confident that the team has recovered. Smiles on having the problem of plenty causing a selection headache and wants his bowlers to bowl with intensity.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. Williamson flips it, Heads is the call by Chandimal but it is a TAIL. NEW ZEALAND ELECT TO BOWL FIRST.

Hello and welcome to the first day of the international home summer for New Zealand. They kick off with a two-Test series against Sri Lanka, the first being in Wellington. The hosts have the upper hand because of the home advantage and the recent away series win against Pakistan in the UAE. On the other hand, Sri Lanka need something special to defeat this New Zealand side. Their recent home series against England was not that good and they need to improve in all departments, especially their batting. Akila Dananjaya's action has been declared illegal but don't think he will be missed too much on the seaming tracks in this country. The Black Caps had announced their playing XI yesterday itself and are going in with three pacers with only one specialist spinner in Ajaz Patel. Hopefully we get some sort of a contest.
